items.title: Relembre a palestra: Além do Go-Live, a camada da adoção digital #SITCWB2026
items.author: AdrianoCWB
items.text:
No dia 7 de novembro, no Auditório Gregor Mendel da PUCPR, Rodrigo Cordeiro, Head de Transformação de Negócios na Numen, apresentou no SAP Inside Track Curitiba 2026 a palestra "Além do Go-Live: Maximizando a Adoção Digital e o ROI com WalkMe". 
 Sobre a palestra 
 Toda transformação SAP tem duas histórias: a do projeto (escopo, orçamento, go-live no prazo) e a do uso real (seis meses depois, parte da equipe ainda usa planilha paralela). Rodrigo mostrou que o gap entre as duas é a distância entre o sistema estar certo e a pessoa saber o que fazer com ele no momento exato. 
 Segundo dados do WalkMe citados na palestra, US$ 104 milhões foram desperdiçados em 2024 com tecnologia subutilizada, cada colaborador perde 51 dias por ano com fricção digital e 70% das iniciativas de transformação não geram o valor planejado. 
 SAP BTM e a camada de adoção 
 O SAP BTM integra três camadas: processos (SAP Signavio), arquitetura (SAP LeanIX) e adoção (WalkMe), que foi o foco da palestra. O WalkMe é uma plataforma de adoção digital que fica sobre a aplicação, sem alterar o código, para identificar onde a pessoa trava e guiá-la na hora. Foi adquirido pela SAP em setembro de 2024 e se apoia em três pilares: dados, ação e experiência. 
 WalkMe e Joule: rivais ou parceiros? 
 A resposta foi que não é um ou outro. A Joule responde "o que eu preciso fazer?" a partir de uma pergunta do usuário. O WalkMe responde "como faço isso nesta tela?", de forma proativa e contextual. Na ideia da palestra, a Joule é o cérebro e o WalkMe é a camada de experiência. 
 Três lentes e o Learning Arc 
 Consultor: garantir que o usuário saiba operar no dia 1 é entrega, escopo e diferencial. 
 Usuário: a ajuda aparece quando ele trava, e não em um treinamento genérico feito meses antes. 
 Líder: a métrica de sucesso deixa de ser "foi ao ar" e passa a ser "está sendo usado direito". 
 Learning Arc: treinamento dentro da aplicação, com simulações em modo Demo, Practice e Test, e medição de conclusão e de quedas em quiz. 
 Para levar 
 Go-live não é a linha de chegada, é o começo do uso real. 
 Adoção digital é uma entrega do projeto, não um detalhe. 
 Meça o uso, não a presença no treinamento. 
 Sobre o palestrante 
 Rodrigo Cordeiro, Head de Transformação de Negócios na Numen e professor de pós-graduação em arquitetura funcional, com nove certificações SAP. 
 Assista à palestra no YouTube (de 1:20 a 40:19 do vídeo): https://youtu.be/6kfJHxQN140?t=80 
 Veja todas as palestras no post índice: https://community.sap.com/t5/curitiba-blog-posts/sap-inside-track-curitiba-2026-relembre-as-palestras-sitcwb/ba-p/14522453

items.title: SAP Business Data Cloud: Transforming Enterprise Data into Intelligent Business Decisions
items.author: sraji2486
items.text:
Introduction 
 Organizations today use different applications to manage their business operations. Finance, procurement, sales, human resources, and other departments generate large amounts of data every day. Although this information is valuable, it is often stored across different systems, making it difficult to get a complete view of business performance. 
 For example, an organization may use SAP S/4HANA for finance and procurement, SAP SuccessFactors for employee information, and SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC) for reporting. When management needs a consolidated report, data from these systems must be connected, prepared, and presented in a meaningful way. 
 This is where SAP Business Data Cloud (SAP BDC) comes into the picture. 
 SAP Business Data Cloud is a cloud-based solution that brings together SAP and non-SAP data, analytics, planning, and AI capabilities. It helps organizations make better use of their existing data while maintaining its business meaning. 
 In this blog, let's explore SAP Business Data Cloud, its key components, how it works, and how it can be used in practical business scenarios. 
 What is SAP Business Data Cloud? 
 SAP Business Data Cloud is a fully managed cloud solution designed to connect and manage business data from different sources. 
 It brings together existing SAP technologies such as SAP Datasphere, SAP Analytics Cloud, and SAP Business Warehouse, along with SAP Databricks and other capabilities. 
 The main idea behind SAP BDC is to make business data available for different purposes without repeatedly creating the same data models and business logic. 
 For example, finance teams can use financial data for reporting, while procurement teams can use purchasing information to analyze supplier performance. Both teams can work with trusted business data while meeting their individual requirements. 
 One important point is that SAP Business Data Cloud is not simply another reporting tool or a replacement for SAP Datasphere. It provides a broader environment that connects data management, analytics, planning, and AI. 
 Key Components of SAP Business Data Cloud 
 SAP Business Data Cloud brings together different technologies, with each component supporting a specific business requirement. 
 SAP Datasphere 
 SAP Datasphere helps organizations connect data from different systems, create data models, and maintain business context. It allows developers to prepare and share data for analytical requirements. 
 SAP Analytics Cloud 
 SAP Analytics Cloud supports dashboards, reporting, data visualization, and enterprise planning. Business users can use it to analyze performance and monitor important KPIs. 
 SAP Business Warehouse 
 SAP BW supports existing enterprise data warehouse requirements. Organizations can continue using their existing BW investments while exploring modernization options through SAP BDC. 
 SAP Databricks 
 SAP Databricks provides capabilities for data engineering, machine learning, data science, and AI. It helps organizations perform advanced analysis using SAP and non-SAP data. 
 SAP HANA Cloud 
 SAP HANA Cloud provides database and data processing capabilities. It also supports application development and advanced analytical requirements. 
 SAP Master Data Governance 
 SAP Master Data Governance helps organizations maintain consistent and reliable master data across business applications. 
 These components work together to provide a connected data and analytics environment. Organizations can select the capabilities based on their requirements and existing technology landscape. 
 Understanding Data Products 
 One of the important concepts in SAP Business Data Cloud is data products. 
 In simple terms, a data product is a prepared collection of business data that can be reused by different teams and applications. 
 In traditional data environments, developers often extract individual tables and create separate models for every reporting requirement. This can result in repeated development work and inconsistent calculations. 
 Data products help reduce this effort by providing structured information with business meaning, metadata, and documentation. 
 For example, consider a finance data product containing general ledger information, company codes, financial documents, and cost centre details. 
 Instead of preparing the same information separately for multiple reports, different teams can use the available data product for their requirements. 
 SAP also provides ready-to-use data products from supported SAP applications, which can help organizations reduce the time required to prepare data. 
 The main benefits are reusability, consistency, better data management, and easier access to trusted business information. 
 Practical Example: Building an Enterprise Analytics Solution 
 Let's consider a company that wants to create a consolidated management dashboard using finance, procurement, and HR information. 
 The company currently uses: 

 SAP S/4HANA for finance and procurement. 

 SAP SuccessFactors for HR. 

 SAP Datasphere for data integration and modelling. 

 SAP Analytics Cloud for dashboards and reporting. 
 The requirement is to bring the required information together and provide management with a single view of business performance. 
 The implementation can be approached in the following way. 
 Step 1: Identify the source systems 
 First, identify the systems and data required for reporting. 
 For example, finance information may include actual expenses, GL balances, and cost centres. Procurement may require purchase orders, supplier details, and invoice information. HR may require employee details and department information. 
 Understanding the source systems and business requirements is important before starting the integration. 
 Step 2: Integrate the required data 
 The next step is to make the required information available through SAP BDC. 
 Depending on the source system and requirement, organizations can use available SAP data products, data federation, replication, and supported integration methods. 
 For example, finance and procurement information can be obtained from SAP S/4HANA, while employee information can be obtained from SAP SuccessFactors. 
 The integration approach should be selected based on data volume, refresh frequency, and business requirements. 
 Step 3: Create data models using SAP Datasphere 
 Once the data is available, SAP Datasphere can be used to prepare the required business models. 
 For example, finance information can be connected with cost centre and company code details to calculate department-wise expenditure. 
 Similarly, procurement information can be organized to analyze supplier performance and purchasing activities. 
 These models help maintain common business definitions and make information available for different reporting requirements. 
 Step 4: Develop dashboards using SAP Analytics Cloud 
 After preparing the data models, SAP Analytics Cloud can be used to develop dashboards. 
 A management dashboard may include: 

 Total revenue and expenses. 

 Actual versus budget. 

 Department-wise expenditure. 

 Purchase order details. 

 Supplier performance. 

 Employee headcount. 
 Management can use these dashboards to understand business performance without checking multiple applications separately. 
 For example, finance managers can compare actual expenses against budget, while procurement managers can review purchasing trends. 
 Step 5: Explore AI and advanced analytics 
 Once the organization has a reliable data foundation, it can explore machine learning and AI capabilities. 
 For example, historical procurement information can be analyzed to identify unusual purchasing patterns or predict future requirements. 
 SAP Databricks can support data engineering and machine learning activities, while SAP's AI capabilities can help users work with business information more effectively. 
 This example shows how different SAP technologies can work together to support an end-to-end analytics requirement. 
 Zero-Copy Data Sharing 
 Another important capability of SAP Business Data Cloud is zero-copy data sharing. 
 In traditional data environments, information is often copied from one platform to another before it can be used for reporting or advanced analysis. This can increase storage requirements and create additional data maintenance activities. 
 SAP Business Data Cloud Connect supports sharing data and metadata between SAP BDC and supported external platforms without creating additional physical copies for supported scenarios. 
 For example, an organization using SAP Databricks for machine learning can access shared SAP business data for advanced analysis. 
 This helps reduce unnecessary data movement and allows organizations to make better use of their existing data platforms. 
 However, zero-copy does not mean that every integration is completely free from data movement. The actual approach depends on the supported platform and integration requirements. 
 SAP BW Modernization 
 Many organizations have been using SAP Business Warehouse for several years. These environments contain important business data, reports, queries, and transformation logic. 
 Replacing the entire BW environment can be expensive and time-consuming. 
 SAP Business Data Cloud provides modernization options that allow organizations to continue using existing BW investments while gradually adopting cloud-based capabilities. 
 For example, an organization using SAP BW for financial reporting can review its existing data models and identify which data assets can be reused through supported SAP BDC integration capabilities. 
 This allows organizations to modernize their data environment step by step instead of replacing everything immediately. 
 The main objective is to protect existing investments while taking advantage of newer data and analytics capabilities. 
 Industry Applications 
 SAP Business Data Cloud can support different industries because most organizations depend on information from multiple business systems. 
 Some practical examples include: 
 Manufacturing: Combining production, inventory, procurement, and financial information to improve operational visibility. 
 Banking: Connecting customer, transaction, and financial information to support risk analysis. 
 Retail: Combining sales, inventory, and customer information to understand demand and improve planning. 
 Healthcare: Connecting financial and operational information to improve resource management. 
 Oil and Gas: Combining maintenance, procurement, workforce, and financial information to understand operational costs. 
 For example, an oil and gas company may want to analyze maintenance expenditure across different operational locations. By combining maintenance, procurement, and finance information, management can compare costs and identify areas that require further investigation. 
 These use cases show how connected business data can support better decisions across different departments. 
 Challenges and Best Practices 
 Although SAP Business Data Cloud provides several capabilities, organizations should consider a few important points before implementation. 
 Data quality: Incorrect or incomplete source data can affect reporting results. Source data should be validated before creating analytical models. 
 Security: Finance, HR, and operational information may have different access requirements. Appropriate roles and authorizations should be maintained. 
 Integration: The integration approach should be selected based on the source system, data volume, and required refresh frequency. 
 Performance: Data models, joins, and refresh schedules should be reviewed to maintain good reporting performance. 
 Skills and knowledge: Implementation teams should understand the relevant SAP technologies, including Datasphere, Analytics Cloud, data integration, and security. 
 It is also better to start with a small business use case, such as finance

items.title: Material Ledger Activity Update 2 → 1 (CON2): Benefit vs. Loss of Multilevel Actual Activity Prices
items.author: Jiecang2024
items.text:
Dear SAP experts, 
 Our users want to see actual activity prices at production order level for cost analysis. We understand that this requires changing the Material Ledger "Activity Update" setting from 2 to 1 and using CON2. The same note states that after the switch, actual activity prices are no longer reflected in the multilevel (material) view and appear only at production order level.( https://me.sap.com/notes/2240562/E ) 

 We would like to understand whether this trade-off is worthwhile before deciding on a switch in production. 
 Planned test approach: Copy production data to a test system after a period has been closed and settled. 
 Switch from 2 to 1 and activate CON2 at the period boundary (previous period closed, new period without postings). 
 Post a few new production orders in the new period, and run price determination, CON2 and settlement. 
 Compare CKM3, cost component split and order variances before and after the switch. 
 We are aware that switching within an open period is not supported, so we only intend to test at a period boundary. 
 Questions 
 1. Benefit: After the switch, what exactly is available at order level that is not available with setting 2 (for example, actual activity prices and activity price differences by order)? Are there any standard reports for this analysis (for example, CKM3 or the cost component split)? 
 2. Loss at material level: Which information is no longer available in the multilevel view after the switch? Does this affect material price determination, inventory valuation, or the actual cost component split of finished and semi-finished goods? 
 Risks: What are the known risks and side effects of the switch, especially for in-process orders, orders spanning the switch period, and TECO orders with errors in COFC or historical goods movement errors (for example, CO688)? 
 3. Prerequisites: Is it mandatory that no open production orders exist at the time of the switch? If some orders cannot be closed, what is the impact? 
 4. Reversibility: Can the setting be switched back from 1 to 2 later? If yes, under which conditions? 
 5.Recommendation: Does SAP recommend this switch only to meet the requirement of order-level actual activity prices? Is there an alternative that provides order-level analysis without losing the multilevel view? 
 6. Testing: Is our test approach (copy after period close, switch at the period boundary) sufficient, or is there an SAP-recommended procedure or checklist for validating the switch? 
 Thank you in advance for your guidance. 
 Best regards

items.title: SAP and planqc Bring Quantum Computing into Business Processes
items.author: SAP News
items.text:
MUNICH — SAP SE (NYSE: SAP) is stepping up its quantum computing activities and expanding its collaboration with Munich-based quantum computer manufacturer planqc. 
 Innovation at SAP helps organizations turn technology into an engine for business innovation 

 Learn more 

 At Quantum Day Munich, which is being run by SAP, the two companies are demonstrating for the first time how a planqc neutral-atom quantum computer can be integrated into an SAP software environment. SAP is also showcasing its first quantum agents and establishing a dedicated quantum team in Munich. Starting in 2027, the companies plan to test initial business scenarios on actual planqc quantum hardware. 

 SAP sees the potential for quantum computing to reach performance levels relevant to SAP software applications before the end of this decade. The company is, therefore, exploring how quantum computing can complement classical optimization, simulation and AI. Munich offers a dense ecosystem of leading research institutions, specialized suppliers, startups and industry partners. 

 “Quantum computing opens up new ways to solve complex problems. We see neutral-atom quantum computers in particular as a promising approach to scalable quantum computing,” said Dr. Carsten Polenz, Global Head of Quantum, SAP. “What matters now is embedding this computing power into business processes and making it accessible to customers. With planqc, we can develop directly on real quantum hardware and shorten the path to real-world business applications.” 

 The technical foundation is a cloud interface connecting the SAP software landscape with planqc’s quantum computing environment. The hybrid architecture combines classical solvers, quantum simulators and real quantum hardware. At today’s Quantum Day Munich, SAP and planqc are demonstrating for the first time how this works successfully in a real-world application scenario. In optimizing the loading of a delivery vehicle, an optimization task is transferred from an SAP software logistics process to the planqc environment and computed on a quantum simulator. The resulting loading plan is then fed back into the SAP software process. In the future, such scenarios are expected to run directly on a neutral-atom quantum computer. 

 On the same technological foundation, SAP is developing its first quantum agents. They are designed to capture business objectives and constraints and orchestrate appropriate solution methods. Users should, therefore, be able to address business problems without having to program quantum hardware themselves or develop specialized quantum expertise. The focus is on the business decision, not the underlying computing technology. 

 “Europe has a strong research base and essential parts of the technology supply chain for quantum computers,” said Dr. Alexander Glätzle, co-founder and CEO of planqc. “The challenge now is to turn these strengths into competitive products and real-world applications. With SAP, we are bringing our neutral-atom quantum computers to where companies manage complex business processes. This allows companies to build expertise and develop real-world use cases while the technology matures, rather than waiting until powerful quantum computers become available.”

items.title: What Is Guided Buying, Really?
items.author: Lars_Elmquist
items.text:
Easy buying isn’t necessarily Guided Buying. 
 An employee can find a laptop, compare models and place an order in minutes. That may be a great user experience. But if they unknowingly bypass the contracted supplier, approved models and security requirements, was it really a good buying experience? 
 That question changed how I think about Guided Buying. 
 My research took me beyond usability and procurement software into governance, choice architecture, buying behaviour and an important feedback loop between employees and Procurement. 
 Guided Buying may be less about helping people find what they want, and more about helping them make an appropriate buying decision.

items.title: Defining Tax Codes for Time-Dependent Taxes in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
items.author: SibiAndavar
items.text:
Introduction 
 Tax regulations are subject to change, and businesses often need to update their tax rates from a specific effective date while continuing to support transactions from earlier periods. Managing such changes correctly in SAP is important to ensure accurate tax determination and avoid inconsistencies in financial postings. 
 Time-Dependent Taxes (TDT) in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition provides a structured way to handle these scenarios by allowing tax rates to be maintained according to their validity periods. This becomes particularly useful when a statutory tax rate changes and the new rate needs to be applied only from a specific date. 
 In this blog, we will explore how Time-Dependent Taxes work, how tax codes and validity periods are maintained, what needs to be considered during configuration, and how the setup can be validated through practical examples. The blog also highlights important considerations for testing tax-rate changes and ensuring that the applicable rate is correctly determined for business transactions. 
 Time-Dependent Taxes (TDT) provides a mechanism to maintain tax codes and tax rates with specific validity periods. Instead of treating a tax-rate change as a completely new configuration scenario, the validity of a tax rate can be managed based on the relevant date. 
 This is particularly useful when a country or region introduces a statutory tax-rate change that becomes effective from a specific date. 
 This describes TDT as a solution that allows tax codes, rates, and related tax-code properties to be maintained with validity periods. Countries with TDT activated can maintain tax rates through SSCUI 101016 – Define Tax Codes for Sales and Purchases. 
 Time-Dependent Taxes allow tax rates to be maintained according to their validity period. 
 For example, consider a tax code with the following rates: Validity Period Tax Rate 
 01.01.2026 – 30.06.2026 18% 
 01.07.2026 – 31.12.9999 20% 
 In this example, the same tax code can have different tax rates depending on the relevant tax determination date. 
 Therefore: 
 Transactions falling within the first validity period are determined with 18%. 
 Transactions falling within the second validity period are determined with 20%. 
 Historical transactions can continue to use the rate applicable during their respective validity period. 
 This approach is particularly useful when legislation changes the tax rate from a predefined effective date. 
 Before maintaining time-dependent tax rates, it is important to check whether Time-Dependent Tax Calculation is active for the relevant country/region. 
 Tax-rate maintenance is only available through the relevant configuration when TDT is active for the country/region. 
 Therefore, the general sequence is: 
 Check TDT availability → Activate TDT where applicable → Maintain tax codes and validity periods 
 Define tax codes for sales and purchases 
 In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, tax codes can be maintained using: 
 SSCUI 101016 – Define Tax Codes for Sales and Purchases 
 Maintain a tax code with a new validity period 
 Consider the following business scenario. 
 A company currently uses tax code V1 with a tax rate of 18% . 
 Due to a statutory change, the tax rate will become 20% from July 1, 2026. 
 Instead of replacing the existing rate, the tax configuration can be maintained using validity periods. 
 The important point is that the existing validity period remains available while a new validity period is introduced for the changed rate. 
 This allows the tax configuration to represent the applicable rate over time 
 Time-Dependent Taxes are also relevant for countries where statutory tax changes need to be reflected in SAP S/4HANA Cloud. 
 For example, India is enabled for Time-Dependent Taxes, allowing customers to maintain tax codes and change tax rates with validity periods when required by legal changes. 
 For an India localization scenario, customers should consider the applicable GST configuration, tax code, tax components, and relevant statutory reporting requirements when introducing or changing a tax rate. 
 The tax configuration should always be aligned with the applicable legal requirement and the relevant SAP localization guidance 
 Conclusion 
 Time-Dependent Taxes provide a structured approach for managing tax-rate changes in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. 
 Instead of treating every statutory tax-rate change as an entirely new tax-code configuration, TDT allows applicable tax rates to be maintained with validity periods. This helps businesses prepare for future legal changes while maintaining the appropriate tax information for different periods.

items.title: How to Monitor Errors and Receive Email Alerts for Asynchronous SOAP API Calls in SAP S/4HANA Cloud
items.author: Zhehui_Xia28
items.text:
Problem Background 
 A customer is using the SOAP service Product Master – Replicate from Client to SAP S/4HANA Cloud (technical name: ProductMDMBulkReplicateRequest_In ) to create and update material master data via API integration. During daily operations, they noticed a critical issue: when an API call fails, no error message is returned in the SOAP response, and no messages appear in any monitoring panel . The customer had no way to detect or investigate failed replications, so they raised a support incident. 
 The root cause lies in how this service works: it is an asynchronous inbound SOAP service . This means that after the external system sends a request, SAP S/4HANA Cloud immediately returns an HTTP acknowledgement — regardless of whether the actual business processing succeeds or fails. Processing errors are logged internally by the SAP Application Interface Framework (AIF) , but those logs are not exposed by default to end users. 
 Solution 
 The issue can be resolved through configuration — no code changes are required. By properly setting up the Assign Recipients to Users app and the Message Dashboard app, users can: 
 View error logs for the Product Master SOAP service in the Message Dashboard. 
 Receive email notifications automatically when an API call encounters a processing error. 
 Analysis Steps 
 Step 1: Assign the AIF Recipient to the User 
 Open the Assign Recipients to Users app (App ID: F2949). Select the target user, choose Assign , and in the dialog, enter the following: 
 Field Value 
 Namespace /CMDPR 
 Recipient Name CMD_PRODUCT 
 Also select the message types the user should be allowed to view, such as Application Error and Technical Error . 
 After saving, the user will be able to see Product Master – Replicate from Client to SAP S/4HANA Cloud error logs in the Message Dashboard app. 

 Note 1 : To access the Assign Recipients to Users app, the user's business role must include the business catalog Communication Management – Message Monitoring Configuration ( SAP_CA_BC_COM_CONF_PC ) . 
 Note 2 : To access the Message Dashboard app, the business catalog Communication Management – Message Monitoring and Error Handling ( SAP_CA_BC_COM_ERR_PC ) is also required. Both are included in the standard business role template Configuration Expert – Business Network Integration ( SAP_BR_CONF_EXPERT_BUS_NET_INT ) . 
 Step 2: Configure Email Notifications in the Message Dashboard 
 Open the Message Dashboard app . Locate the Product Master – Replicate from Client to SAP S/4HANA Cloud interface entry. Click the notification icon in the Notification column and set it to E-Mail for Every Single Error . From this point on, every time an API call results in a processing error, an email alert will be sent automatically. 
 Note : Before configuring email notifications, verify that the target user has a valid email address maintained in the Maintain Business Users app. Without a maintained email address, notifications cannot be delivered. 

 Once configured, the email notification you receive will look like this: 

 Subject : An interface raised an alert that requires your attention. 
 Error while processing interface /<NAMESPACE> - <INTERFACE_NAME> - <VERSION> 
 Work instruction 
 Check for temporary errors 
 Check for missing master data and customizing 
 Check for data related errors – update the payload where permitted 
 Check for data related errors – if payload cannot be edited, cancel the messages and ask the sender system to resend an updated message 
 URL to the interface or message https://<your-system>.s4hana.cloud.sap/sap/bc/ui2/flp#AIFMessage-startMessageMonitoringIntegrationExperts?ns=... 
 The email directly includes a deep link to the failing interface in the Message Dashboard, so you can click straight through to investigate the error without manually searching. 
 Reference : For the full documentation on the Assign Recipients to Users app, see Assign Recipients to Users – SAP Help Portal . 
 Reference : For the Product Master SOAP service API monitoring documentation, see Product Master – Replicate from Client to SAP S/4HANA Cloud – SAP Help Portal . 
 Broader Applicability 
 This configuration approach applies to all asynchronous inbound SOAP APIs in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition that are registered with the SAP Application Interface Framework (AIF). Each such API has its own specific Namespace and Recipient Name, documented on the respective API's SAP Help page under the API Monitoring and Error Handling section. 

 Note : This mechanism applies specifically to asynchronous SOAP services. For synchronous SOAP services, errors are returned directly in the SOAP response payload and do not require AIF monitoring configuration. 
 Reference : For the complete list of alert notification options supported by SAP Application Interface Framework (including email, SAP Alert Notification Service for BTP, and SAP Fiori push notifications), see Alert Notification – SAP Help Portal . 
 Conclusion 
 By reading this article and several similar scenario blogs I've written previously, I hope you now understand how to configure the SAP Application Interface Framework to surface error logs and receive email alerts for asynchronous SOAP API calls in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition — without requiring any custom development. 
 You can find more information about SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition topics at the following link: SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition – SAP Community 
 If you have any suggestions or thoughts about this article, please feel free to share them in the comments section. I look forward to communicating with you. You are also welcome to follow my personal account, and I look forward to seeing you in the next blog post!

items.title: 如何在 SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 中监控异步 SOAP API 错误并接收邮件通知
items.author: Zhehui_Xia28
items.text:
问题背景 
 某客户使用 SOAP 服务 Product Master – Replicate from Client to SAP S/4HANA Cloud （技术名称： ProductMDMBulkReplicateRequest_In ）通过 API 集成方式新增和修改物料主数据。在日常运营中，客户发现了一个严重问题：当 API 调用失败时， SOAP 响应中没有任何错误信息，标准监控面板中也看不到任何报错记录 ，导致无法感知和排查失败的复制请求。为此，客户提报了支持事件。 
 问题的根本原因在于该服务的工作机制：这是一个 异步入站 SOAP 服务（Asynchronous Inbound SOAP Service） 。外部系统发送请求后，SAP S/4HANA Cloud 会立即返回 HTTP 确认，不论后续业务处理是否成功。处理错误由 SAP Application Interface Framework（AIF） 在内部记录，但默认情况下，这些日志对最终用户不可见。 
 解决方案 
 此问题可通过纯配置解决，无需任何自定义开发。通过正确配置 给用户分配收件人 应用和 消息仪表盘 应用，用户可以实现： 
 在消息仪表盘中查看 Product Master SOAP 服务的 错误日志 ； 
 在 API 调用出现处理错误时，自动接收 邮件提醒 。 
 分析步骤 
 步骤一：为用户分配 AIF 收件人 
 打开 给用户分配收件人（Assign Recipients to Users） 应用（应用 ID：F2949）。选择目标用户，点击 分配（Assign） ，在弹出对话框中填入： 
 字段 值 
 命名空间（Namespace） /CMDPR 
 收件人名称（Recipient Name） CMD_PRODUCT 
 同时勾选用户可查看的消息类型，例如 应用程序错误（Application Error）和技术错误（Technical Error） 。 
 保存后，该用户即可在 消息仪表盘 中查看 Product Master – Replicate from Client to SAP S/4HANA Cloud 的错误日志。 

 注意 1 ：访问 给用户分配收件人 应用需要用户的业务角色包含业务目录 Communication Management – Message Monitoring Configuration（ SAP_CA_BC_COM_CONF_PC ） 。 
 注意 2 ：访问 消息仪表盘 应用还需要业务目录 Communication Management – Message Monitoring and Error Handling（ SAP_CA_BC_COM_ERR_PC ） 。以上两个业务目录均包含在标准业务角色模板 Configuration Expert – Business Network Integration（ SAP_BR_CONF_EXPERT_BUS_NET_INT ） 中。 
 步骤二：在消息仪表盘中配置邮件通知 
 打开 消息仪表盘 应用。找到 Product Master – Replicate from Client to SAP S/4HANA Cloud 对应的接口条目，点击 Notification 列中的 通知图标 ，将其设置为 每次单个错误发送邮件（E-Mail for Every Single Error） 。配置完成后，每当 API 调用出现处理错误，系统将自动发送邮件提醒。 
 注意 ：配置邮件通知前，请确认目标用户在 维护业务用户（Maintain Business Users） 应用中已维护了有效的电子邮件地址，否则通知无法送达。 

 配置成功后，收到的邮件通知格式如下： 

 主题（Subject） : An interface raised an alert that requires your attention. 
 Error while processing interface /<命名空间> - <接口名称> - <版本号> 
 Work instruction 
 Check for temporary errors 
 Check for missing master data and customizing 
 Check for data related errors – update the payload where permitted 
 Check for data related errors – if payload cannot be edited, cancel the messages and ask the sender system to resend an updated message 
 URL to the interface or message https://<your-system>.s4hana.cloud.sap/sap/bc/ui2/flp#AIFMessage-startMessageMonitoringIntegrationExperts?ns=... 
 邮件中包含一个 直接跳转链接 ，点击即可在消息仪表盘中定位到对应的报错接口，无需手动搜索，大幅提升排查效率。 
 参考文档 ：给用户分配收件人应用完整说明，请参见 Assign Recipients to Users – SAP Help Portal 。 
 参考文档 ：Product Master SOAP 服务的 API 监控说明，请参见 Product Master – Replicate from Client to SAP S/4HANA Cloud – SAP Help Portal 。 
 适用范围 
 此配置方案适用于 SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 中 所有通过 SAP Application Interface Framework（AIF）注册的异步入站 SOAP API 。每个此类 API 都有其特定的 Namespace 和 Recipient Name，可在各自 API 的 SAP Help 页面的 API Monitoring and Error Handling 章节中找到。 

 注意 ：此机制仅适用于 异步（Asynchronous） SOAP 服务。对于同步（Synchronous）SOAP 服务，错误信息会直接在响应体中返回，无需配置 AIF 监控。 
 参考文档 ：SAP Application Interface Framework 支持的完整告警通知方式，请参见 Alert Notification – SAP Help Portal 。 
 总结 
 通过阅读本文以及我之前撰写的类似场景博客，希望你现在已了解如何通过配置 SAP Application Interface Framework，在 SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 中查看异步 SOAP API 的错误日志并自动接收邮件告警，从而在无需任何自定义开发的情况下有效监控 API 集成异常。 
 更多关于 SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 的内容，欢迎访问： SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition – SAP Community

items.title: Support Custom (Non-GS1) Barcode Prefixes and Parsing Rules in Warehouse Management (WM) RF Apps
items.author: Madhavan_R1
items.text:
In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, Warehouse Management (WM) mobile RF transactions currently restrict barcode decoding to international GS1 standards. There is no standard configuration or extensibility option in Public Cloud to handle non-GS1 custom barcode identifiers or an option to programmatically strip custom prefixes (such as legacy warehouse prefixes, supplier-specific identifiers, or proprietary internal prefixes) during RF scanning. 
 While SAP provides barcode parsing configuration activities ( Define Settings for Scanner Hardware and Define Barcode Parsing ) for Inventory Management, these settings are restricted to a limited set of IM-based Fiori apps and do not extend to WM RF transactions. 
 In real-world manufacturing and distribution environments, especially during Brownfield-to-Public-Cloud transitions or across multi-warehouse networks, organizations frequently receive and manage inventory labeled with legacy or third-party non-GS1 barcodes. Without native parsing or prefix-stripping capabilities in WM RF, customers are forced to rely on hardware-level scanner programming. This workaround is brittle and unsustainable because: 
 Hardware dependency: Older or mixed fleets of RF scanners often lack the capability to conditionally strip variable prefixes, forcing unplanned capital expenditure to replace otherwise functional hardware. 
 High IT maintenance overhead: Maintaining complex, site-specific prefix-stripping rules across dozens of physical devices and multiple warehouses (each with its own label variations) creates severe configuration drift and support bottlenecks. 
 Operational disruption: If a scanner resets or a new supplier label format is introduced, warehouse floor operations stall until IT manually updates every device. 
 Can SAP introduce native, Clean Core-compliant support for custom barcode prefix handling and parsing within SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition? Specifically, SAP could address this gap through one or more of the following capabilities: 
 Extend Define Barcode Parsing to WM RF: Allow the existing IM barcode parsing framework ( Define Barcode Parsing ) to be assigned and executed within WM RF logical transactions and verification profiles. 
 Allow Maintenance of Bar Code Specification for Non-GS1 Prefixes: Expand the WM RF barcode specification configuration to support custom, user-defined prefixes and delimiters (e.g., stripping fixed or variable-length character prefixes before field validation) alongside standard GS1 Application Identifiers (Equivalent to the functionality available in Private cloud). 
 Release a Cloud-Ready Developer Extensibility BAdI: Provide a released, cloud BAdI (equivalent to the On-Premise/Private Cloud BAdI /SCWM/EX_BARC_DECODE) that allows customers to implement custom decoding and prefix-stripping logic for RF input fields such as Product, Batch, Handling Unit, and Serial Number. 
 Currently, there appears to be no option in Public Edition to handle this and I am curious to know how this is handled by other customers running on Public Cloud? Is there any workaround available? 
 I have also logged a Customer influence request here - https://cis.influence.sap.com/ideas/CIS2897-I-1397 
 Thank you, 
 Madhavan

items.title: In-House Repair (3XK) with Warehouse Management: how to pick spare parts before repair confirmation?

items.text:
Hi Experts, 
 I'm evaluating In-House Repair (3XK) with Warehouse Management in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, release [2608] (source: SAP Road Map Explorer ). The Plant and storage location used in my tests are mapped to a warehouse number, spare parts are kept in warehouse-managed storage bins and used through the repair order. 
 What I see in my tests: 
 The outbound delivery is only created when the repair confirmation is completed, with or without final confirmation. After that, I create and confirm the warehouse task and post GI. 
 In practice, technicians need the parts at the workbench before they start the repair, so picking happens too late in the flow. 
 If I complete the confirmation with final confirmation, the repair order becomes Completed. Parts can't be adjusted if something changes during the repair. 
 If I complete it without final confirmation, the repair order stays Released. However, every additional completed repair confirmation creates a new outbound delivery. I couldn't find a check that stops the same parts from being picked or goods-issued twice. 
 Questions: 
 Is there a standard way to create the outbound delivery or warehouse task earlier , so parts can be picked before the repair starts? For example, at repair order release, or from the material reservation. 
 Is there any standard check that blocks a second delivery or GI for parts that were already picked? 
 What does SAP recommend when parts change mid-repair? (since outbound delivery is only created after repair confirmation completion). This includes putting unused parts back into a bin, adjusting quantities, and adding unplanned items. 
 Any experience from similar implementations would be very helpful. 
 Thanks in advance! 
 Claudia

items.title: How to Access Additional HTTP Headers Configured in SAP BTP Destinations from RAP (ABAP Cloud)?
items.author: Gayathri_Vedagiri
items.text:
Hi Experts, 
 I am working on an integration between an SAP BTP ABAP Cloud RAP application and SAP Build Process Automation (BPA), where I need to trigger a BPA process through an HTTP destination configured in SAP BTP. 
 I have maintained the required configuration in the BTP destination under Additional Properties , including: 

 URL.headers.irpa-api-key 

 URL.queries.environmentId 

 HTML5.DynamicDestination 

 WebIDEUsage 

 Other destination-related properties. 
 Scenario in CAP: 
 In my CAP application, when I consume the destination, the additional properties configured in the BTP destination are handled automatically. For example, custom HTTP headers such as irpa-api-key are automatically included in the outgoing request without explicitly setting them in the application code. 
 Scenario in RAP (ABAP Cloud): 
 I am implementing the same integration in an ABAP Cloud RAP application using the HTTP client and destination service. 
 However, the custom header configured through URL.headers.irpa-api-key is not automatically added to the outgoing HTTP request. 
 Currently, I have to manually retrieve the API key and explicitly set the header in my ABAP implementation: 
 lo_request->set_header_field(
 i_name = 'irpa-api-key'
 i_value = lv_irpa_api_key
). 
 I then execute the HTTP POST request: 
 lo_response = lo_http_client->execute(
 i_method = if_web_http_client=>post
). 
 My Questions: 

 Is there a standard mechanism in ABAP Cloud RAP to automatically read and apply custom HTTP headers configured under Additional Properties in an SAP BTP destination? 

 Does the ABAP Cloud HTTP client or destination service support automatic propagation of custom headers such as URL.headers.irpa-api-key , similar to the behavior observed in CAP? 

 If automatic propagation is not supported, is there a recommended API or approach to retrieve these additional destination properties dynamically in ABAP Cloud? 

 What is the recommended way to maintain and consume sensitive configuration values such as BPA API keys centrally through BTP destinations without hardcoding them or maintaining duplicate configurations in ABAP code? 
 I would like to reuse the existing BTP destination configuration in RAP, just as I do in CAP, rather than maintaining the same API key separately. 
 Has anyone implemented a similar scenario in ABAP Cloud RAP? Any guidance, recommended APIs, or working code examples would be greatly appreciated. 
 Thanks in advance for your suggestions!

digest.headline: Thin day: ABAP Cloud practice without the trial, async SOAP error alerting in S/4HANA Cloud, and unanswered BAdI and destination-header questions.
digest.overview:
The most useful item for ABAP developers is a blog on practising ABAP Cloud now that the Developer Trial can't be downloaded or extended. The author ran the ABAP Cloud readiness check on a classic program in an S/4HANA 2023 development system and got 23 findings, then 0 after a rewrite. The post shows neither code nor findings. The questions do show real gaps: reading BTP destination properties from ABAP Cloud, STO pricing with the BAdI limited to SUPPLIER and PLANT, and a field missing from an OData V2 API. deep_dives.title: Using ABAP Cloud readiness checks as a learning loop
deep_dives.explanation:
With the ABAP Cloud Developer Trial unavailable, the post [7] proposes using an existing S/4HANA 2023 development system, where ABAP Cloud rules are active. The author wrote a classic-style program, ran the ABAP Cloud readiness check and got 23 findings. After rewriting it the ABAP Cloud way, the check gave 0 findings and the program ran. The post doesn't list the findings, so this is a method, not a catalogue.

To reproduce it, build a report that deliberately breaks the rules. Use a direct `SELECT` on a non-released table, an obsolete statement, a call to a non-released function module or class, and classic list output. Run the readiness check, group the findings by cause, and fix each group. Typical fixes are released CDS views or released APIs instead of tables, and released classes instead of unreleased ones. These are standard ABAP Cloud practices, not details from the post.

The value is that findings become a measurable exercise: the finding count falls as each category is fixed, and the end state is a program that runs under ABAP Cloud language version rules. Use a sandbox package, not a productive one.

deep_dives.title: Destination properties and HTTP headers in ABAP Cloud
deep_dives.explanation:
The question [71] describes a destination with Additional Properties such as `URL.headers.irpa-api-key` and `URL.queries.environmentId`. In CAP these are added to outgoing requests automatically. In ABAP Cloud RAP the developer reads the key and sets it with `set_header_field` on an `if_web_http_client` request before calling `execute( i_method = if_web_http_client=>post )`.

The thread asks for a standard API to read the additional properties and a way to avoid duplicating the secret in ABAP code. No answer is given, so don't assume automatic propagation exists. Check the current documentation for the destination-to-HTTP-client path your release uses.

Whatever mechanism is used, the design goal is clear: the secret lives in the destination or a communication arrangement, and not in the source code, constants or a custom table.

deep_dives.title: Verifying what a BAdI or released API actually exposes
deep_dives.explanation:
Two questions show the same trap. In [19], BAdI `PRCG_DOC_ITEM_CONDITION_AMOUNT` provides only `SUPPLIER` and `PLANT`, but the pricing rule needs the sending storage location. A `SELECT` on the order fails because it isn't saved yet at pricing time. In [39], `CustomerRequirementType` is missing from the `I_SalesDocumentItem` OData V2 entity.

The check order is the same each time. First read the interface or signature of the extension point, then the CDS view in ADT, then the service's exposed properties in `$metadata`. A field can exist in the CDS view and not in the API. If the view has it, an extension or a custom projection with a service definition and binding is the route [39]. If the BAdI doesn't pass the data, any alternative must be verified against SAP documentation, because [19] has no answer.

The older user exit question [50] follows the same pattern: find the calling program with where-used, then check copy control before coding.

post_drafts.text:

The HTTP reply is only an acknowledgement.
Errors end up in AIF, and users don't see them by default.

1. App F2949: assign the AIF recipient (example: /CMDPR, CMD_PRODUCT)

3. Make sure the user has a valid e-mail

interview_questions.question: The ABAP Cloud Developer Trial is unavailable. How would you prepare a team to learn ABAP Cloud restrictions using an existing S/4HANA 2023 system?
interview_questions.answer: An S/4HANA 2023 development system already has ABAP Cloud rules active, so it can serve as a practice environment. I would create a sandbox package and write a classic-style program with typical violations: direct selects on non-released tables, non-released API calls and obsolete statements. Then I would run the ABAP Cloud readiness check and record the findings. The team fixes them by category until the count reaches zero, as one blog went from 23 to 0. The fixes use released CDS views and released APIs. Finally, confirm the program runs under the ABAP Cloud language version. Use a sandbox package so nothing productive is touched.

interview_questions.question: Async inbound SOAP calls to S/4HANA Cloud return success but the data isn't replicated. How do you diagnose and monitor this?
interview_questions.answer: Async inbound SOAP returns an HTTP acknowledgement before business processing, so the response says nothing about the result. Processing errors are logged in AIF, which end users don't see by default. I would use the Message Dashboard to find the failed entry. For proactive alerts, assign an AIF recipient to the user in Assign Recipients to Users (F2949), using the namespace and recipient from the API's documentation, for example /CMDPR and CMD_PRODUCT for the product master service. Then set the interface notification to 'E-Mail for Every Single Error'. The user also needs a valid e-mail address in Maintain Business Users. Synchronous services return errors in the response and don't need this.

interview_questions.question: A BAdI doesn't pass a field you need, and a released OData API lacks a field. How do you decide where to change?
interview_questions.answer: I first confirm what each layer provides. For the BAdI, I read its interface signature. In the STO pricing case, PRCG_DOC_ITEM_CONDITION_AMOUNT gives only SUPPLIER and PLANT, and the order isn't saved, so selecting from the database fails. I would look for another extension point or data source, and verify it against SAP documentation. For the API, I open the CDS view in ADT and compare it with the service's $metadata, because a field can exist in the view and be absent from the API. If the view has it, I would use an extension or a custom projection with a service definition and binding. If it doesn't, the field isn't available at that layer. I don't design before this check.
